implemented_requirements.evidence: constants.BOARD_SIZE = 15 and Board.__init__(self, size=BOARD_SIZE) creates a 15x15 grid.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Two players (black and white) alternate placing stones
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.__init__ sets current_player = BLACK; make_move switches player after a successful move.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Stone placement validation (inside board and empty cell)
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.is_valid_move checks bounds via is_inside and that grid cell equals EMPTY.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Win detection for five aligned stones horizontally, vertically, or diagonally
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.get_winning_line iterates over DIRECTIONS (horizontal, vertical, both diagonals) and returns a line when length >= STONES_TO_WIN (5).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Draw detection when board is full
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.is_full scans for any EMPTY cell; Game.make_move sets state to DRAW if board.is_full() and no win.

implemented_requirements.requirement: GUI rendering of board, stones, last move marker, winning line highlight, and restart button
implemented_requirements.evidence: gui.py defines GomokuGUI with draw_board, draw_stones (highlights winning_line and last_move), and a Restart button that calls Game.reset.

implemented_requirements.requirement: User interaction via mouse clicks to place stones
implemented_requirements.evidence: GomokuGUI.on_click converts click coordinates to board positions and calls Game.make_move.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Status message indicating current player, win, or draw
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.get_status_message returns appropriate text; GUI updates a label with this message.

judge.summary: All core Gomoku features are present: a 15x15 board, alternating black/white moves, validation, win/draw detection, and a functional Tkinter GUI with click handling, status updates, and restart capability. The code appears syntactically correct and likely runnable, so the submission meets the benchmark.
